Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used in machine learning to minimize a model's loss function by iteratively adjusting its parameters. It works by taking steps in the direction opposite to the gradient of the loss function, effectively moving "downhill" toward a minimum (Page 24). 

While traditional gradient descent computes the gradient using the entire training dataset (full batch gradient descent), variants like stochastic gradient descent (SGD) use subsets of data (mini-batches) to make the process computationally efficient, especially with large datasets (Page 74). This makes SGD particularly effective for large-scale machine learning problems (Page 238). Although gradient descent may not always reach a global or even local minimum, it often finds a sufficiently low value of the cost function to be practical (Page 169).
